entries.title: Genesis 29:3
segments: Were all the flocks gathered--they rolled--watered--put the stone again; these words describe what was the daily custom.

entries.title: Genesis 29:4
segments: A kind and courteous behavior is most likely to receive kindness in return; and a disposition to be useful, most likely to make a man welcome, and give him success.

entries.title: Genesis 29:7
segments:
High day; the sun is yet high. 
 
  Be gathered together; that is, for the night.

entries.title: Genesis 29:8
segments: We cannot; either because they had not bodily strength till more of the shepherds should come, or because it was contrary to established usage.

entries.title: Genesis 29:11
segments: Men sometimes weep for joy, and few things are more affecting to a truly thankful heart, than the great goodness of God.

entries.title: Genesis 29:12
segments: Her father's brother; Jacob was Laban's sister's son; of course not his brother in our sense of the word, but his nephew.

entries.title: Genesis 29:14
segments: My bone and my flesh; my near relative.

entries.title: Genesis 29:15
segments: Our relatives, as well as others, should be fairly paid for their services; and we ought not to wish any to labor for us without receiving a just compensation.

entries.title: Genesis 29:20
segments: One of the most prompt, cheerful, pleasant, and persevering springs of action, is love.  Under its influence, labor, sacrifices, and self-denials often give great delight.

entries.title: Genesis 29:23
segments: He took Leah; it was then customary for a bride to be taken at night to her husband covered with a veil.

entries.title: Genesis 29:25
segments:
Beguiled; imposed on, deceived.  Jacob had deceived his father, and now his wife's father deceived him. 
 
Those who wickedly deceive others should not wonder if others deceive them, and they experience the evils of it through life.

entries.title: Genesis 29:27
segments: Fulfil her week; Leah's week; that is, a week of feasting, according to the custom of weddings, after which Rachel would be given to him, on condition of his serving Laban seven years more.

entries.title: Genesis 29:31
segments: Was hated; regarded less than Rachel.

entries.title: Genesis 29:32
segments: Reuben; meaning, see a son.  The Lord hath seen my affliction, and given me a son.

entries.title: Genesis 29:34
segments: Levi; joined--thinking that her husband would now be joined in affection to her, as he was to Rachel.

entries.title: Genesis 29:35
segments:
Judah; praise--she being disposed to praise the Lord for his goodness. 
 
God often regards those whom men wrongfully disregard, and graciously bestows such favors upon them as to fill their hearts with gratitude, and open their mouths in praise.
